item.title: Bce valuta nuove reti di sicurezza in euro per rafforzarne ruolo globale
item.description: La Banca centrale europea intende ampliare le reti di sicurezza in euro per agevolare l’accesso alla valuta unica da parte delle banche centrali estere, nel tentativo di rafforzare il ruolo internazionale dell'euro.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La Banca centrale europea intende ampliare le reti di sicurezza in euro per agevolare l’accesso alla valuta unica da parte delle banche centrali estere, nel tentativo di rafforzare il ruolo internazionale dell'euro. Lo ha detto la presidente della Bce Christine Lagarde. L'iniziativa arriva in un contesto caratterizzato da timori relativi alla frammentazione finanziaria e alla crescente incertezza sul futuro del dollaro statunitense sotto la presidenza Trump. Lagarde ha affermato che la Bce lavorerà sulle linee di swap, strumenti che forniscono liquidità d'emergenza nei momenti di crisi consentendo alle banche centrali estere di prendere in prestito euro in cambio della propria valuta. "Lavoreremo sulle linee di swap affinché rispondano meglio all’imperativo di garantire la sovranità della zona euro e la forza dell’euro", ha detto Lagarde ai parlamentari europei. Le linee di swap alleviano la pressione per i prenditori esteri di fondi, ma prevengono al contempo che tensioni finanziarie all’estero si ripercuotano sulla zona euro. La Bce ha accordi di questo tipo con la Federal Reserve e con le banche centrali di Giappone, Regno Unito, Canada e Svizzera. L’iniziativa rientra negli sforzi costanti della Bce per accrescere il peso internazionale dell’euro. La Bce ha ricevuto quasi 30 richieste di adesione ad un'altra struttura di finanziamento, noto come operazioni pronti contro termine, o repo – che consente alle banche estere di ottenere liquidità in prestito a fronte di garanzie in euro. Funzionari delle banche centrali e investitori temono che la Federal Reserve possa tagliare le proprie linee di swap, che attualmente rappresentano il principale strumento di sostegno globale per migliaia di miliardi di dollari di finanziamenti erogati al di fuori degli Stati Uniti.

item.title: White House weighs red-dyed diesel tax relief to lower fuel prices
item.description: The White House is considering regulatory relief that would allow broader sales of red-dyed diesel as part of an effort to bring down soaring prices, a move that could allow some buyers to avoid the federal fuel tax, according to two people familiar with the discussions.
item.dc:creator: Jarrett Renshaw, Nicole Jao
item.content:encoded: The White House is considering regulatory relief that would allow broader sales of red-dyed diesel as part of an effort to bring down soaring prices, a move that could allow some buyers to avoid the federal fuel tax, according to two people familiar with the discussions. The red-dye proposal has emerged from days of administration deliberations as one of the leading alternatives to a diesel export ban, which has been discussed as global supply disruptions drive prices to record levels. [USN:SPN45A01C TEXT:"President Donald Trump has backed"] a ban, but that has faced widespread opposition from the oil industry and other parts of the business community. The Trump administration is looking for ways to bring down diesel prices without disrupting fuel supplies or creating additional costs elsewhere in the economy, under growing pressure to ease fuel costs as November's midterm elections approach and Trump's economic approval ratings remain under strain. The administration has also been seeking voluntary commitments from major refiners to limit diesel exports, Reuters reported last week, as officials weigh alternatives to a government-imposed export ban. Energy Secretary Chris Wright has contacted executives at several major refiners to gauge their willingness to engage in such an action. A White House official said no final decisions have been made, but the president is weighing all options to lower prices. Trump told a Fox News reporter on Sunday while attending the Presidents Cup golf tournament in Illinois that he is "very seriously" weighing a ban on diesel exports. “That can oftentimes lead to a little bit of an increase in gasoline for cars, so we’re looking at it very seriously. We may do it,” he added. RED DYE PLAN The tax proposal would expand the circumstances under which red-dyed diesel, which is generally reserved for off-road uses such as farming and is exempt from most federal fuel taxes, could be sold for broader use, the people said. The administration is weighing the proposal as Trump seeks to ease fuel costs that have climbed sharply in recent weeks. Under current federal rules, the tax on highway diesel is 24.4 cents per gallon, while dyed diesel is exempt from that tax but remains subject to a 0.1-cent-per-gallon charge that funds the federal Leaking Underground Storage Tank Trust Fund. Allowing wider sales of dyed diesel could reduce the federal tax burden on eligible purchases, although the impact on the price paid by consumers would depend on how the relief is structured and how much of the savings is passed through by fuel sellers. Farm Belt lawmakers are also pressing the administration and Congress to act as high diesel prices squeeze farmers heading into harvest, when fuel is a major operating cost. US Representative Ashley Hinson, a Republican running for the Senate in Iowa, has called for the House to return to Washington before the midterm elections and pause diesel exports and suspend the federal gas tax, while also proposing a diesel relief program for farmers and truckers. Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy, said the proposal would not address the supply imbalances that have driven up on-road diesel prices. Farmers already use untaxed dyed diesel, he noted, while allowing truckers to use the fuel could save them the federal tax without increasing diesel supplies. "I can't think that this would have any impact at all," De Haan said. "It's simply diesel with red dye added that's not taxed. It does nothing to improve supply or impact price." The idea comes as several states have moved to relax restrictions on dyed diesel amid surging fuel costs. Alabama, Louisiana and Nebraska have each taken temporary steps in recent days to allow broader use of the tax-exempt fuel or suspend state penalties, while Alabama and Louisiana have sought additional relief from the federal government. The potential move comes as the national average price of diesel has climbed above $6 a gallon, putting more pressure on farmers, truckers and other businesses that rely on the fuel.

item.title: GRANOS Futuros de la soja en Chicago caen al quedar excluida de recortes arancelarios de China
item.description: Los futuros de soja de la Bolsa de Chicago se desplomaban el lunes debido a la liquidación de posiciones largas, ante la decepción de los operadores por el hecho de que la soja quedara excluida de los recortes arancelarios propuestos para los productos agrícolas tras la cumbre de la semana pasada entre Donald Trump y Xi Jinping.
item.dc:creator: P.J. Huffstutter
item.content:encoded: Los futuros de soja de la Bolsa de Chicago se desplomaban el lunes debido a la liquidación de posiciones largas, ante la decepción de los operadores por el hecho de que la soja quedara excluida de los recortes arancelarios propuestos para los productos agrícolas tras la cumbre de la semana pasada entre Donald Trump y Xi Jinping. [USN:L6N45K09T TEXT:"Según el acuerdo"], China y Estados Unidos han acordado reducir los aranceles impuestos a productos importados entre ambos países por valor de 60.000 millones de dólares, en una amplia gama de productos que van desde el maíz estadounidense hasta los electrodomésticos chinos. También abarca una amplia gama de otros productos agrícolas estadounidenses, como el trigo, el sorgo y los aceites vegetales -incluidos el aceite y la harina de soja-, junto con la carne, los productos lácteos y otros artículos, según la lista de reducción arancelaria publicada conjuntamente por el Ministerio de Comercio de China y la Casa Blanca. Sin embargo, China, el principal importador mundial de soja, omitió este producto, que constituye la mayor exportación agrícola de Estados Unidos a China. Los operadores de materias primas llevaban días esperando noticias sobre el acuerdo y el hecho de que la soja quedara fuera de la lista se consideró un factor significativamente bajista para los futuros de soja del CBOT, según los analistas de mercado. Una serie de otras presiones lastraron los mercados de cereales y semillas oleaginosas, desde la fortaleza de los rendimientos de los bonos y del dólar estadounidense hasta la subida de los precios del petróleo tras el rechazo por parte de Trump de un acuerdo de paz con Irán. La noticia de que el maíz y el trigo se incluyeran en la lista de productos sujetos a aranceles reducidos por parte de China tampoco supuso un gran apoyo durante la sesión bursátil, según los operadores, ya que se considera que Pekín tiene una demanda limitada de esos cereales procedentes de Estados Unidos. El contrato de soja de Chicago más negociado de forma continua cayó hasta los 12,7925 dólares por bushel en un momento dado, el precio más bajo desde el 31 de agosto, y registraba un descenso del 2,46% hasta situarse en 12,8650 dólares por bushel a las 1529 GMT. Este mes, el contrato de referencia alcanzó su máximo en casi tres años en vísperas de la reunión entre Washington y Pekín. Los futuros del maíz de la CBOT bajaban un 1,51%, a 5,2025 dólares el bushel, aunque se mantuvieron por sobre los mínimos de un mes alcanzados el viernes. Los futuros de trigo de la CBOT caían un 2,28%, a 6,8725 dólares el bushel. El mercado del trigo siguió centrado en los esfuerzos diplomáticos para aliviar las interrupciones en las exportaciones de cereales del mar Negro, indicaron los operadores, a pesar de que continuaban los ataques diarios en la guerra que Rusia mantiene con Ucrania.

item.title: UK first-time buyer scheme lifts housebuilders, but success hinges on design
item.description: Britain's new first-time buyer support scheme could provide the biggest boost to housebuilders in years, helping revive sales that have languished since the previous "Help to Buy" programme ended in 2023.
item.dc:creator: Raechel Job, Simone Lobo, Yadarisa Shabong
item.content:encoded: Britain's new first-time buyer [USN:L6N45I066 TEXT:"support scheme"] could provide the biggest boost to housebuilders in years, helping revive sales that have languished since the previous "Help to Buy" programme ended in 2023. But investors and analysts say much will depend on next month's budget, which will set out who qualifies for support and where it can be used. The "Your First Home" programme is designed for first-time buyers who can afford mortgage payments but have struggled to save deposits amid high rents and broader cost-of-living pressures. Buyers will need deposits of just 2.5%, while the government will provide loans of up to 20% of a property's value, allowing them to qualify for mortgages that would otherwise require larger deposits. The loans will have an initial interest-free period. Details including income thresholds and regional price caps are due when new finance minister John Healey delivers his first budget on October 28. Housebuilder shares [USN:L6N45K0EC TEXT:"rallied"] on Monday as investors bet the scheme could unlock pent-up demand and support new-home sales. Britain has been without a government-backed buyer support scheme since "Help to Buy" ended in March 2023, the longest gap in such support for decades. Developers have lobbied hard for its return as high borrowing costs and affordability pressures weighed on demand. "Overall, I think this could help stimulate volumes in the housebuilding market," said James Thorne, fund manager at Columbia Threadneedle, a shareholder in homebuilder Crest Nicholson and some building materials suppliers. DEVIL IN THE DETAILS The biggest question is whether the scheme is broad enough to stimulate demand while remaining targeted at lower-income buyers. Unlike "Help to Buy", the new programme will include income caps and tighter price restrictions aimed at concentrating support on those deemed most in need. Analysts said the design of the caps would determine how much demand the scheme generates, particularly in higher-priced parts of southern England. Peel Hunt analyst Sam Cullen said the two biggest unknowns were the level of regional price caps and how regions would be defined. The previous scheme used England's nine standard regions, but Cullen said builders sometimes struggled where affluent areas fell within lower-cap regions or straddled regional boundaries. The new programme will also require developers to contribute financially, raising concerns that smaller builders could struggle to participate. "Its success will largely be dependent upon the parameters set in terms of household income, house price and developer contribution limits," said Steve Turner, executive director of the Home Builders Federation. "Help to Buy" drew support from builders because it was accessible to a broad range of buyers and developers, Turner added. Richard Donnell, executive director at property website Zoopla, said boosting first-time buyer purchasing power would help, but increasing housing supply remained equally important. "The greatest impact on housing delivery will come if it is accompanied by more homes being built at the price points and in the sizes first-time buyers are looking for," he said. Analysts identified Persimmon (PSN.L) and MJ Gleeson (GLEG.L) , both heavily exposed to first-time buyers, among the likely winners. Building materials companies such as bricks supplier Ibstock (IBST.L) could benefit even sooner, as construction activity typically rises before homes are sold. "The parts of the market likely to see the greatest benefit are brick suppliers and other areas of the supply chain, which should benefit from that volume growth," Thorne said.

item.title: Prosecutors reopen investigation into alleged 2024 gang rape at Cornell University
item.description: New York state prosecutors have reopened an investigation into an alleged 2024 gang rape at a Cornell University fraternity house, a district attorney confirmed on Monday, after a civil lawsuit filed this month by the alleged victim sparked renewed outrage.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Ax
item.content:encoded: New York state prosecutors have reopened an investigation into an alleged 2024 gang rape at a Cornell University fraternity house, a district attorney confirmed on Monday, after a civil lawsuit filed this month by the alleged victim sparked renewed outrage. In a lengthy statement, Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten confirmed that his office would present the case against seven alleged perpetrators to a grand jury for a possible indictment. He also sought to explain why prosecutors did not pursue criminal charges two years ago, saying that the lawsuit's allegations differed from the alleged victim's original account in 2024. The woman, who prosecutors have not named, gave a statement to campus police at the time, according to Van Houten, that "described her drug use and sexual conduct as voluntary, conscious and consensual." The alleged victim's lawyer, Thomas Giuffra, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. He told CNN in a statement that the police report was "not materially different" from the civil lawsuit's claims and criticized the district attorney's office for not pursuing a more thorough investigation sooner, the network reported. The lawsuit, filed against the seven Chi Phi fraternity members, Cornell University and several other defendants, asserted that the woman, then a 20-year-old student at Cornell, was "plied with alcohol and drugs to the point of intoxication" by fraternity members, leaving her unable to consent before she was sexually assaulted. Members of the fraternity used a Snapchat group chat to encourage others to join in, according to the lawsuit, which included a photo of some messages as well as details about the alleged assault itself. In a statement, a Cornell spokesperson said the school supports Van Houten's decision and noted that the chapter of Chi Phi involved in the case has remained barred from campus since 2024. Cornell previously conducted an investigation into the allegations that resulted in "a range of sanctions, which included expulsions and suspensions from Cornell." "Any suggestion that the university did not impose consequential punishments for those involved is false," said the spokesperson, Kyle Kimball. It was not immediately clear if all of the fraternity members named in the lawsuit have legal representation. Jeremy Saland, a defense lawyer who represents one of the members, said in a statement that his client had done nothing more than respond to the chat with an immature comment and that his client "welcomes any further investigation by the district attorney." In the US, fraternities are college-based clubs for male students, often sharing a house together. The national Chi Phi fraternity, which was founded more than two centuries ago, did not immediately respond to an emailed request for comment.

item.title: Cravath private equity leader returns to Weil
item.description: Weil, Gotshal & Manges is bringing back two leading lawyers in private equity and restructuring who previously departed for rival law firms as it navigates a string of recent partner exits.
item.dc:creator: Sara Merken
item.content:encoded: Weil, Gotshal & Manges is bringing back two leading lawyers in private equity and restructuring who previously departed for rival law firms as it navigates a string of recent partner exits. Peter Feist is returning to Weil as US co-head of its private equity practice from Cravath, Swaine & Moore, where he led the private equity group, Weil said on Saturday. Feist left Weil for Cravath in 2023. His clients have included Advent International, OMERS Private Equity and Providence Equity Partners, according to his Weil online biography. He was not immediately available for comment on Monday. Last week Weil said that Debra Sinclair, who was US co-chair of the strategic capital and restructuring department at Willkie, Farr & Gallagher, would be joining the firm in the coming weeks. Sinclair was previously an associate at Weil. Sinclair did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Weil said her recent work has included leading a team that advised Saks Global through its Chapter 11 restructuring. Weil has lost a handful of other partners in recent weeks. Cravath said earlier this month that it had [USN:L6N4530WP TEXT:"hired"] leading New York dealmaker Michael Aiello, who led Weil's corporate department, alongside five other partners including Weil's M&A practice co-leader Matthew Gilroy. Other departures from the firm in recent weeks have included the co-head of its private equity group, Chris Machera, who joined Paul Weiss; US private funds group co-head Stephanie Srulowitz, who joined Simpson Thacher; and global white-collar defense co-head Daniel Stein, who joined Freshfields. Sullivan & Cromwell brought on David Avery-Gee, Weil's London M&A leader and co-managing partner of its London office, alongside partner Sarah Flaherty.

item.title: LeBron soaks in the brotherly love in Philly media debut
item.description: "You guys know who I am, right?"
item.dc:creator: Amy Tennery
item.content:encoded: "You guys know who I am, right?" The name is familiar but the 76ers red, white and blue jersey was new for LeBron James, who opened his introductory press conference on Monday with a quick quip amid the extraordinary buzz that surrounds his arrival in Philadelphia. Wearing the Sixers jersey in public for the first time, he quickly removed his own name tag from the table as he met with an overflowing crowd of reporters at the Sixers training complex, where his arrival has been regarded as nothing short of a coronation. "I'm super excited to get in front of these fans, they know sports," said James, with a clean-shaven head to match his clean start with his fourth franchise, following a successful tenure with the Los Angeles Lakers. "They know ball." The 41-year-old four-times MVP took a [USN:L6N43219Q TEXT:"historic pay cut"] - and left behind his own [USN:L1N3LZ005 TEXT:"son-turned-teammate Bronny"] - to begin his record-extending 24th season with a team he is convinced can lift the trophy. Fans hope he is right, with the glory days of Julius "Dr. J" Erving, who brought home their last title in 1983, an ever-distant memory. "If we want to accomplish something that's really, really important, like if we say that we want to do something special will be a collective sacrifice," said James, whose reported $8 million two-year contract in Philadelphia pales in comparison to the roughly $52 million he made in his final season in Los Angeles. He told reporters he had a list of five teams that he was considering before landing on Philadelphia, insisting he had not decided whether his contract with the Sixers would be the last of his career. "I'm just looking at it every single day on how I can be the best version of myself for this franchise while I'm here," he said. EMBIID, LEBRON TEAM UP James, who also picked up titles in Miami and Cleveland, will form a formidable cast with the 2023 MVP and big man Joel Embiid, who debuted a slimmer physique after years of injury issues. "Joel is one of the most talented guys that we have in the world and, and obviously we all know that, you know, for him it's been about help. You know, how can you stay healthy to be the best version of himself, be the best version of himself, to be the best version of us as a team," said James. Asked what his own off-season conversations looked like getting James to Philadelphia, the seven-times All-Star Embiid flashed a wry smile. "I didn't talk to LeBron at all," he said. "I didn't recruit him." James begins his record-extending 24th season on the road against the [USN:L6N42J14M TEXT:"reigning champion"] New York Knicks, who ended 53 years of heartbreak for the five boroughs [USN:L6N42J1EI TEXT:"in June"].

item.title: Primeira-ministra da Itália supera desafio das eleições suplementares contra novo rival de extrema-direita
item.description: A coalizão governista da Itália venceu, nesta segunda-feira, uma eleição suplementar muito aguardada na região da Calábria — o primeiro grande teste para a primeira-ministra Giorgia Meloni contra um novo adversário de extrema-direita, antes das eleições gerais previstas para o próximo ano.
item.dc:creator: Angelo Amante
item.content:encoded: A coalizão governista da Itália venceu, nesta segunda-feira, uma eleição suplementar muito aguardada na região da Calábria — o primeiro grande teste para a primeira-ministra Giorgia Meloni contra um novo adversário de extrema-direita, antes das eleições gerais previstas para o próximo ano. O partido Futuro Nacional, liderado pelo ex-general do Exército Roberto Vannacci, subiu para cerca de 9% nas pesquisas de opinião desde seu lançamento em fevereiro, ultrapassando os parceiros menores da coalizão de Meloni e desafiando a direita no eleitorado conservador de Reggio Calabria. No entanto, a tentativa do partido não deu certo: o candidato do governo obteve cerca de 53% dos votos, enquanto o candidato de Vannacci conquistou aproximadamente 10%, segundo uma contagem parcial. Analistas haviam previsto um desempenho mais forte para Vannacci nesse reduto tradicionalmente de direita, afirmando que ele poderia ter dividido o voto da direita e entregue a vitória à centro-esquerda. “Vencemos por uma maioria esmagadora”, afirmou Roberto Occhiuto, governador da Calábria e vice-líder do partido da coalizão Forza Italia, em um vídeo publicado no X. IMAGEM MANIPULADA POR IA O apoio a Vannacci cresceu em todo o país devido à sua retórica antimigrante e aos apelos ao que ele descreve como valores tradicionais italianos. Sua ascensão deixou Meloni inquieta e pode complicar suas perspectivas de reeleição, afastando eleitores que apoiaram sua coalizão na última votação nacional, em 2022. Pesquisadores afirmaram que ela poderia manter o poder se formasse uma aliança com Vannacci. Mas qualquer parceria desse tipo causaria tensão nas fileiras do governo. A subsecretária do Parlamento, Matilde Siracusano, deputada do Forza Italia e companheira de Occhiuto, alertou que qualquer pacto eleitoral com o Futuro Nacional representaria “um problema sério”. Ela afirmou que processará Vannacci depois que ele postou nas redes sociais uma imagem gerada por IA mostrando-a vestindo uma blusa decotada e reveladora. O candidato de centro-esquerda na eleição suplementar obteve cerca de 35% dos votos, superando o desempenho do bloco em 2022, embora a participação do eleitorado tenha sido de apenas 22%, contra 49,4% há quatro anos. “Com uma participação eleitoral extremamente baixa, forte atenção da mídia e um candidato com apoio pessoal significativo, acredito que Vannacci esperava um resultado muito melhor”, disse Lorenzo Pregliasco, diretor da empresa de pesquisas YouTrend. O próprio Vannacci não comentou imediatamente o resultado.

item.title: Italian court convicts three Egyptians for kidnapping slain student Regeni
item.description: An Italian court on Monday convicted three Egyptian security officials of involvement in the 2016 kidnapping of student Giulio Regeni, whose tortured body was found days after his disappearance in Cairo.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: An Italian court on Monday convicted three Egyptian security officials of involvement in the 2016 kidnapping of student Giulio Regeni, whose tortured body was found days after his disappearance in Cairo. The three men were sentenced to 10 years in jail, while a fourth Egyptian defendant was acquitted. Regeni, a postgraduate student at Britain's Cambridge University, vanished in the Egyptian capital on January 25, 2016. His body was found almost a week later, with a post-mortem showing he had been extensively tortured before his death. In a ruling read out to the court, a judge said Major Magdi Sharif, from Egypt's General Intelligence, police Colonel Hisham Helmy and Colonel Ather Kamal, a former head of investigations in Cairo were guilty of the "aggravated kidnapping" of Regeni. The judge acquitted Major General Tarek Sabir, the former head of state security, of the same charge and also dismissed the accusation of "conspiracy to commit aggravated murder" leveled against Sharif. Prosecutors had sought a life term for Sharif and 17 years and six months in jail for the other three. "We achieved this result despite what can be described as less than wholehearted cooperation from the Egyptian authorities," Rome Chief Prosecutor Francesco Lo Voi told reporters. The four men were tried in absentia under Italian legislation allowing the prosecution of crimes committed abroad against Italian citizens. They have never publicly responded to the accusations and Egypt has denied any state involvement in Regeni's death. Italian and Egyptian prosecutors initially investigated the case together, but the two sides later fell out and came to very different conclusions. The Egyptians blamed the murder on a gang of criminals, who were subsequently killed in a shootout with police. Italian prosecutors argued that Regeni was abducted and tortured by Egyptian security officials because of his academic research into trades unions, a sensitive subject in Cairo.

item.title: Instinct, empresa de agentes de IA, quadruplica de valor após captação de US$1 bi
item.description: A empresa de inteligência artificial Instinct anunciou nesta segunda-feira que levantou US$1 bilhão em sua última rodada de financiamento, quadruplicando seu valor de mercado para US$10 bilhões, impulsionada pelo crescente interesse em IA autônoma.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A empresa de inteligência artificial Instinct anunciou nesta segunda-feira que levantou US$1 bilhão em sua última rodada de financiamento, quadruplicando seu valor de mercado para US$10 bilhões, impulsionada pelo crescente interesse em IA autônoma. A rodada atraiu investimentos de Sequoia Capital, Benchmark Capital e Coatue. O fundador da startup, Noah Shinn, disse ao Wall Street Journal no mês passado que a Instinct havia levantado US$250 milhões com uma avaliação de US$2,5 bilhões. A Instinct está desenvolvendo um agente pessoal capaz de realizar tarefas do dia a dia de forma autônoma. A empresa foi fundada em 2025 por Shinn, que anteriormente trabalhou na Sierra, uma startup de atendimento ao cliente com IA dirigida pelo co-presidente da Salesforce, Bret Taylor. A IA agentiva está atraindo grande interesse de investidores de capital de risco, que apostam que esses agentes poderão, no futuro, automatizar fluxos de trabalho inteiros tradicionalmente realizados por funcionários ou aplicativos de software. A empresa afirma que seus usuários podem se comunicar com o Instinct por mensagens de texto ou chamadas e solicitar que ele cuide de tarefas como planejar viagens, fazer compras de supermercado, reservar ingressos e cancelar assinaturas. “Esse financiamento nos ajuda a levar o Instinct a mais pessoas e a continuar construindo o futuro da IA pessoal”, disse Shinn em comunicado. O Instinct agora está se expandindo para além das tarefas digitais com um serviço de concierge que também pode ligar para empresas em nome do usuário para fazer reservas, informou a empresa. (Por Utkarsh Shetti)

item.title: Associações de casas de apostas vão ao STF para suspender proibição imposta por Lula
item.description: Entidades que representam empresas do setor de apostas online recorreram nesta segunda-feira no Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) para suspender os efeitos da medida provisória editada pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva que proibiu totalmente as chamadas "bets" no país.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Entidades que representam empresas do setor de apostas online recorreram nesta segunda-feira no Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) para suspender os efeitos da medida provisória editada pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva que proibiu totalmente as chamadas "bets" no país. A Associação Nacional de Jogos e Loterias e o Instituto Brasileiro de Jogo Responsável defendem que a MP tenha sua eficácia suspensa até sua apreciação pelo Congresso Nacional, ou até o julgamento final do pedido pelo STF, o que, na prática, manteria a autorização de funcionamento nesse período. As duas organizações entraram com o pedido em uma ação que corre no Supremo desde setembro de 2024 que questionava regras das apostas esportivas. O relator da ação é o ministro Luiz Fux. No recurso, as entidades alegam que não haveria nenhuma urgência que justificasse a edição da medida provisória pelo governo, chegando a falar em "ruptura abrupta" de um setor que estava em funcionamento. "Não há alteração fática que demonstre o aumento substancial ou agravamento de situação não monitorada pelo poder público que justifique uma medida de urgência dessa magnitude", ressaltou o pedido. Lula anunciou na sexta-feira a proibição das operações de apostas online no país, na mais recente de uma série de medidas reveladas antes da eleição do próximo mês. Candidato à reeleição, Lula está em disputa acirrada com o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) antes do primeiro turno de 4 de outubro, de acordo com as pesquisas de intenção de voto. A Advocacia-Geral da União (AGU) apresentou uma manifestação ao STF para que o órgão e a Presidência da República se manifestem em um prazo de 72 horas às alegações apresentadas pelas entidades.

item.title: Fuerzas progubernamentales etíopes afirman haber tomado una localidad estratégica de Tigré
item.description: El ejército de Etiopía y las milicias aliadas se han hecho con el control de la estratégica localidad de Alamata, al sur de la capital de Tigré, informó el lunes una milicia progubernamental, lo que ha supuesto un giro en la situación tras la ofensiva de la oposición lanzada desde la región la semana pasada.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El ejército de Etiopía y las milicias aliadas se han hecho con el control de la estratégica localidad de Alamata, al sur de la capital de Tigré, informó el lunes una milicia progubernamental, lo que ha supuesto un giro en la situación tras la ofensiva de la oposición lanzada desde la región la semana pasada. Un video publicado por la progubernamental Fuerza de Paz de Tigré en su página de Facebook mostró a soldados desfilando por las calles, ondeando banderas etíopes. Reuters no pudo verificar de inmediato la grabación. Dos fuentes diplomáticas también afirmaron que la localidad había caído, mientras que una tercera señaló que las fuerzas progubernamentales habían entrado en ella, aunque aún no estaba claro si tenían el control total. Una fuente vinculada a las fuerzas de la oposición declaró a Reuters que se estaban retirando de Alamata y que esperaban que la ciudad quedara bajo el control del ejército federal en cuestión de horas. Los portavoces del ejército etíope y del Frente Popular de Liberación de Tigré (TPLF), que lidera la resistencia armada contra el Gobierno federal, no respondieron de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios. La toma de Alamata supondría un gran impulso para las fuerzas federales en su avance hacia la capital regional, Mekelle, situada a unos 120 kilómetros al norte. Alamata, un importante centro de abastecimiento de tropas, alimentos y combustible situado cerca de la frontera sur de Tigré con la vecina región de Amhara, cambió de manos en varias ocasiones durante la guerra civil de 2020-2022. Los combates que se han producido desde el miércoles en Tigré y en las regiones vecinas de Amhara y Afar han hecho añicos un acuerdo de paz de cuatro años de antigüedad, el Acuerdo de Pretoria, que puso fin a los enfrentamientos que se cobraron la vida de cientos de miles de personas. La guerra civil de 2020-2022 se originó a raíz de la ruptura de las relaciones entre el TPLF —un movimiento guerrillero convertido en partido político que dominó la política etíope durante casi tres décadas— y Abiy Ahmed, cuyo nombramiento como primer ministro en 2018 puso fin al dominio del TPLF.

item.title: POINT MARCHÉS L'Europe termine sans direction, prudence sur l'Iran
item.description: Les Bourses européennes ont terminé sur de faibles variations lundi, effaçant leurs gains observés plus tôt, la prudence s'imposant face à la pression sur le marché obligataire et les cours pétroliers après le refus par Donald Trump du plan de paix iranien.
item.dc:creator: Coralie Lamarque
item.content:encoded: Les Bourses européennes ont terminé sur de faibles variations lundi, effaçant leurs gains observés plus tôt, la prudence s'imposant face à la pression sur le marché obligataire et les cours pétroliers après le refus par Donald Trump du plan de paix iranien. À Paris, le CAC 40 (.FCHI) a grappillé 0,01% à 8.078,48 points. À Francfort, le Dax (.GDAXI) a cédé 0,01% et à Londres, le FTSE 100 (.FTSE) a reculé de 0,10%. L'indice EuroStoxx 50 (.STOXX50E) a progressé de 0,11% et le Stoxx 600 (.STOXX) a stagné, tandis que le FTSEurofirst 300 (.FTEU3) a lâché 0,04%. Les investisseurs sont en alerte concernant les négociations entre Washington et Téhéran, dans l'optique de voir les craintes inflationnistes s'atténuer. Alors que le président américain Donald Trump a rejeté samedi le plan de paix iranien proposé en marge de l'Assemblée générale des Nations Unies la semaine dernière, un responsable au fait des négociations a indiqué [USN:S8N3UH04Z TEXT:"lundi"] à Reuters que les États-Unis et l'Iran devraient s'entretenir séparément avec des médiateurs d'ici mardi. Bien que les négociations ne semblent pas au point mort, le marché obligataire et les cours pétroliers restent à cran, le Brent étant en passe d'enregistrer une hausse mensuelle proche de 20%, tandis que le rendement du Trésor américain à dix ans culmine à plus de 5,2%. Tandis qu'aucun indicateur économique majeur n'était à l'ordre du jour, la publication des données sur l'inflation dans les principales économies devraient permettre dans les prochains jours de mesurer les risques inflationnistes et d'évaluer les perspectives de politique monétaire. En attendant, les investisseurs interprètent également les propos tenus par la présidente de la Banque centrale européenne (BCE), Christine Lagarde, qui a déclaré [USN:L6N45K0TV TEXT:"lundi"] qu'une "réponse mesurée" restait appropriée pour contenir l'inflation. "Nous anticipons une hausse de l’inflation, mais ne voyons pour l’instant aucun signe indiquant qu’elle s’installe durablement", a-t-elle déclaré lors d'une audition devant une commission du Parlement européen à Bruxelles. "Cela signifie que, même si le choc est trop important pour être ignoré, nous estimons qu’une réponse mesurée est appropriée pour contenir l’inflation", a-t-elle ajouté. Selon les données LSEG, les marchés anticipent à 55% la probabilité d'un maintien des taux à l'issue de la prochaine réunion de la BCE, fin octobre. VALEURS À Paris, Kering (PRTP.PA) et Hermès (HRMS.PA) ont progressé respectivement de 2,2 et de 2,5%, terminant en tête du CAC 40. TotalEnergies (TTEF.PA) a fini quasi inchangé (+0,01%) alors que le géant pétrolier et gazier français tenait sa journée investisseurs. À WALL STREET À l'heure de la clôture en Europe, le Dow Jones (.DJI) perd 0,69%, le Standard & Poor's 500 (.SPX) recule de 0,77% et le Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) abandonne 0,89%. AUCUN INDICATEUR MAJEUR PUBLIÉ LUNDI CHANGES Les cambistes suivent avec intérêt les évolutions des perspectives de politique monétaire au fil des négociations entre Washington et Téhéran, tandis que le billet vert se dirige vers sa plus forte hausse mensuelle depuis juin. Le dollar gagne 0,24% face à un panier de devises de référence (.DXY) , tandis que l'euro perd 0,21% à 1,1367 dollar . TAUX En l'absence de progrès diplomatiques pour en finir avec le conflit au Moyen-Orient et ses répercussions inflationnistes, la pression reste vive sur le marché obligataire, en particulier aux États-Unis et au Royaume-Uni. Le rendement des Treasuries à dix ans grimpe de 8,5 points de base à 5,2656% et le deux ans de 8,3 points de base à 4,9472%. Le Gilt britannique à 30 ans bondit de 6,1 points de base à 5,9237%, tandis que le dix ans a atteint 5,441% soit son plus haut niveau depuis juillet 2007. Le rendement du Bund allemand à dix ans est resté stable à 3,6446%, tout comme le deux ans (+0,1 point de base) à 3,2998%. Le rendement de l'OAT à dix ans a avancé de 0,3 point de base à 4,7739%, tandis que le deux ans a lâché 0,1 point de base à 3,6265%. PÉTROLE Les cours pétroliers poursuivent leur escalade, alimentée par le rejet de la part du président américain Donald Trump du plan de paix iranien qui prévoyait une réouverture du détroit d'Ormuz, dont la fermeture entrave l'approvisionnement mondial en brut. Le Brent gagne 3,26% à 107,72 dollars le baril et le brut léger américain (West Texas Intermediate, WTI) prend 3,3% à 95,46 dollars. item.title: Líder de extrema derecha francesa Bardella desmiente denuncia de medios sobre comentarios antisemitas
item.description: El líder de la extrema derecha francesa, Jordan Bardella, desmintió el lunes un reportaje de la web de investigación Mediapart en el que se le acusaba de haber realizado comentarios antisemitas en mensajes privados hace más de una década, calificando las acusaciones de "burdas invenciones".
item.dc:creator: Michel Rose
item.content:encoded: El líder de la extrema derecha francesa, Jordan Bardella, desmintió el lunes un reportaje de la web de investigación Mediapart en el que se le acusaba de haber realizado comentarios antisemitas en mensajes privados hace más de una década, calificando las acusaciones de "burdas invenciones". La noticia surge en un momento en que el partido de extrema derecha de Bardella, el Agrupación Nacional (RN), cuya candidata presidencial, Marine Le Pen, lidera las encuestas de cara a las elecciones del año que viene, intenta desmontar su imagen racista y establecer estrechos vínculos con Israel. "Desmiento formalmente las acusaciones vertidas contra mí por Mediapart, que me atribuye comentarios delirantes y antisemitas que supuestamente hice cuando era menor de edad. Se trata, evidentemente, de burdas falsedades", escribió Bardella en X. Dijo que había dado instrucciones a su abogado para que emprendiera "todas las acciones legales necesarias" contra Mediapart. En un reportaje publicado el lunes, Mediapart dijo haber revisado decenas de mensajes privados de entre 2013 y 2015 —los primeros años de la carrera de Bardella en el Frente Nacional, precursor del RN— que, según el medio, revelaban un patrón de retórica antisemita y conspirativa. Mediapart citó un mensaje en el que, según el medio, Bardella afirmaba que "todos los bancos son propiedad de judíos". El medio de tendencia de izquierda, que cuenta con una larga trayectoria en el descubrimiento de escándalos políticos en Francia, dijo haber verificado de forma independiente la autenticidad de los mensajes privados y haberse basado también en testimonios de antiguos compañeros de partido, a los que identificó por su nombre de pila y la inicial de su apellido. Bardella, de 31 años, se ha convertido en el rostro del esfuerzo que lleva una década realizando el RN para "desdemonizar", o normalizar, su imagen. Fue el candidato presidencial de facto del partido hasta julio, cuando un tribunal de apelación autorizó a Le Pen a presentarse a la presidencia, y será el primer ministro de Francia si ella gana las elecciones del año que viene. Le Pen, en declaraciones a periodistas el lunes, dijo que cree que el informe "solo podía ser una falsedad, una manipulación, una jugarreta". Agregó que esperaba que Bardella presentara inminentemente una demanda por difamación, y añadió que no tenía nada que discutir con su joven protegido. Una encuesta del lunes la situaba en primera posición en la primera vuelta de las elecciones de abril próximo y le daba la victoria frente a los candidatos de izquierda y de centro en una segunda vuelta en mayo. Una avalancha de comentarios antisemitas, islamófobos y racistas por parte de algunos candidatos del RN echó por tierra las esperanzas del partido de obtener la mayoría parlamentaria en las elecciones legislativas francesas de 2024. Bardella se comprometió entonces a evitar ese tipo de "errores de selección" en el futuro, expulsando sistemáticamente a cualquier candidato con un historial de declaraciones tóxicas.

item.title: Europe’s electric future needs a battery industry of its own
item.description: Europe cannot afford to depend on others for the batteries that will power its economy – and increasingly help defend it.
item.dc:creator: Ann Mettler
item.content:encoded: Europe cannot afford to depend on others for the batteries that will power its economy – and increasingly help defend it. Batteries are becoming a general-purpose technology of the electrified age. They power electric vehicles and stabilise electricity grids. They are increasingly essential to robotics, autonomous systems, drones and defence. Like semiconductors before them, their strategic importance extends far beyond the industries with which they were originally associated. And as electrification becomes the north star of energy security, resilience and decarbonisation, Europe needs a meaningful battery industry of its own. The collapse of Northvolt , the Swedish battery manufacturer that came to embody Europe’s ambitions, should force a rethink of how we build that industry, not whether we need it. As Catalyse Europe outlines in its new report, Europe’s Electric Backbone , the lesson is to build a resilient ecosystem rather than place too much hope in a single champion. Europe’s struggle to scale its battery industry tells a wider story about dependency in a geopolitical environment that has fundamentally changed. Just one company, CATL, supplies roughly 40% of the world’s EV batteries. Chinese companies collectively account for nearly three-quarters of supply. Such concentration matters because batteries are no longer merely an automotive supply chain. Gao Huan, CTO of Chinese battery giant CATL, presents new products ahead of the Auto China show, in Beijing, China, in April this year. CATL, supplies roughly 40% of the world’s EV batteries REUTERS/Maxim Shemetov Ukraine has demonstrated how rapidly modern warfare is becoming electrified. Drones, communications, surveillance, autonomous systems and robotics all depend on batteries. In her recent State of the Union address, Ursula von der Leyen linked access to critical raw materials for batteries and defence to Europe’s independence and security. Battery supply chains are becoming defence supply chains. Europe has also learned that excessive dependence on imported energy carries enormous economic and geopolitical costs. That may one day be as true for imported batteries from China as it was for natural gas imports from Russia. Europe’s current position was not inevitable. The European Battery Alliance was launched in 2017 because policymakers understood what was coming. But Europe struggled to turn ambition into industrial scale. It focused heavily on individual projects and companies – in contrast to China, which built an ecosystem spanning critical minerals and refining, materials and components, battery cells and recycling, supported by investment in research, skills and manufacturing, strategically deployed subsidies and enormous domestic demand. Europe has around 252 gigawatt hours (GWh) of potential battery-cell manufacturing capacity, but much of that capacity is backed by non-European companies, while the wider supply chain remains heavily dependent on China. The next three years will be decisive. Without a supportive policy framework, European companies will cease operations, investments will move elsewhere and industrial capabilities already built will disappear. Europe will struggle to compete with China on price alone. So it needs to become comfortable with paying what might be called a “sovereignty premium” for critical technologies. That does not mean writing blank cheques or permanently insulating European manufacturers from competition. A sovereignty premium should buy demonstrable resilience and industrial capability at a time when companies remain under pressure to innovate, reduce costs and improve productivity. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen delivers the State of the European Union address to the European Parliament, in Strasbourg, France, September 16, 2026. The address linked access to critical raw materials for batteries and defence to Europe’s independence and security. REUTERS/Yves Herman Europe also needs local-content requirements, predictable production support and sustained funding for research and manufacturing. The Industrial Accelerator Act is an important step, but it will not be sufficient without corresponding changes to trade and state-aid policy. Deeper partnerships with trusted countries such as South Korea and Japan – and, hopefully, the United States – should be cultivated while identifying where Europe has genuine technological and industrial strengths. Above all, Europe must bridge the persistent gap between inventing technologies and manufacturing them competitively. Public support cannot end with research or a first factory. If a technology is strategically important, Europe must ensure companies can manufacture it at scale and at cost. European companies also need to pull together rather than compete for the same limited pools of public funding while global competitors build integrated industrial ecosystems. Demand-creation is the missing link. European procurement and local-content provisions can support domestic production. Partnerships between battery producers, automotive manufacturers, defence companies and other industrial users can help technologies reach scale. And as Europe spends hundreds of billions strengthening its defence capabilities, batteries should be recognised as essential security hardware. All this will cost money. But inaction also has a cost: deeper and possibly irreversible dependencies, factories and investment moving elsewhere, and technological knowledge and talent following them. Ultimately, it means further erosion of Europe’s industrial base and political sovereignty. Northvolt should mark a turning point, not an endpoint. Europe should learn from what went wrong, build an ecosystem rather than bet on individual champions, and recognise batteries for what they have become: critical infrastructure for an electrified economy.

item.title: Corteva, Inari settle US dispute over seed patents during trial
item.description: Agricultural technology giant Corteva Agriscience has settled a lawsuit accusing startup rival Inari Agriculture of illegally obtaining and copying its patented corn and soybean seeds, the companies said in a filing in Delaware federal court.
item.dc:creator: Blake Brittain
item.content:encoded: Agricultural technology giant Corteva Agriscience (CTVA.N) has settled a lawsuit accusing startup rival Inari Agriculture of illegally obtaining and copying its patented corn and soybean seeds, the companies said in a filing in Delaware federal court. The companies resolved the case days into a trial in Delaware that had started on September 23 Corteva and Inari asked the court late Sunday to dismiss the case with prejudice, which means it cannot be refiled The filing did not disclose financial terms of the settlement but said that Inari would destroy all Corteva seeds and other biological materials in its possession Spokespeople for the companies did not immediately respond to requests for comment or for more information about the settlement on Monday Corteva sued Inari in 2023 Inari denied the allegations and argued the patents were invalid Corteva spun off from DowDuPont in 2019 The case is Corteva Agriscience LLC v. Inari Agriculture Inc, US District Court for the District of Delaware, No. 1:23-cv-01059. item.title: Cita de Trump con los CEO de IA buscará hallar equilibrio: presidente Cámara de Representantes EEUU
item.description: La reunión que celebrará el martes el mandatario de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, con los presidentes ejecutivos de empresas tecnológicas sobre inteligencia artificial se centrará en hallar un equilibrio entre la innovación y la supervisión, dijo el presidente de la Cámara de Representantes, Mike Johnson.
item.dc:creator: Katharine Jackson
item.content:encoded: La reunión que celebrará el martes el mandatario de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, con los presidentes ejecutivos de empresas tecnológicas sobre inteligencia artificial se centrará en hallar un equilibrio entre la innovación y la supervisión, dijo el presidente de la Cámara de Representantes, Mike Johnson. "No necesitamos una moratoria. No debemos precipitarnos y regular esto en exceso, porque perderíamos la carrera frente a China", afirmó Johnson el lunes en una entrevista con Fox Business Network. "Es importante que la innovación continúe, pero tenemos que encontrar el equilibrio adecuado. De eso tratará la conversación". La reunión en la Casa Blanca, a la que asistirá Johnson, se da mientras las principales empresas de IA están pidiendo frenar el desarrollo de sistemas cada vez más capaces, advirtiendo de los riesgos para la humanidad y haciendo un llamado a los gobiernos para que colaboren en la gestión de esta tecnología. Trump ha restado importancia a las preocupaciones sobre un uso indebido de la IA que pueda perjudicar a las personas, al tiempo que ha subrayado la importancia de mantener la ventaja competitiva ante China. Asimismo, afirma que su país cuenta ya con medidas de control para esta tecnología, incluso en el Departamento de Justicia. Johnson abogó por tener en cuenta la seguridad, pero sin obstaculizar el desarrollo de la tecnología. "Creo que el Departamento de Justicia podría intervenir si las cosas se tuercen, pero lo que necesitamos antes de llegar a esa fase es transparencia y cierta supervisión", dijo en el programa "Mornings with Fox Business". Legisladores de ambos partidos han cuestionado el enfoque de "no intervención" de Trump, incluso a pesar de que la tecnología suscita temores sobre la seguridad, la pérdida de puestos de trabajo y la concentración de poder en manos de un puñado de empresas tecnológicas. El líder demócrata de la Cámara de Representantes, Hakeem Jeffries, señaló que los líderes del sector de la IA están pidiendo a gritos alguna medida gubernamental y que el Congreso tiene la responsabilidad de proteger al pueblo estadounidense. "Por lo tanto, en lo que respecta a la seguridad de la IA, me parece evidente que debemos actuar con audacia y responsabilidad, y hacerlo ahora", comentó a la CNBC el lunes.

item.title: GB Cinq suspects d'un projet d'attentat contre une base de la RAF libérés sous caution
item.description: La police britannique a interrogé lundi cinq hommes suspectés de projet terroriste avant d'annoncer leur libération sous caution, au lendemain de leur interpellation près d'une base aérienne utilisée par les États-Unis pour mener des frappes contre l'Iran.
item.dc:creator: Toby Shepheard
item.content:encoded: La police britannique a interrogé lundi cinq hommes suspectés de projet terroriste avant d'annoncer leur libération sous caution, au lendemain de leur interpellation près d'une base aérienne utilisée par les États-Unis pour mener des frappes contre l'Iran. Le chef des services antiterroristes, Laurence Taylor, a déclaré lors d'une conférence de presse que les suspects faisaient toujours l'objet d'une enquête et que plusieurs pistes restaient à l'étude, y compris la possibilité qu'un ou plusieurs individus agissant pour le compte d'un État étranger aient été impliqués dans le projet présumé. La police a arrêté les cinq hommes tôt dimanche matin après avoir été alertée par une agricultrice que trois grandes camionnettes blanches se dirigeaient vers la base aérienne de la Royal Air Force (RAF) de Fairford, dans l'ouest de l'Angleterre, qui abrite des bombardiers américains effectuant des missions contre l'Iran. "Pour être très clair, (la libération sous caution des suspects) ne signifie pas que l'enquête est terminée", a déclaré Laurence Taylor devant le siège de la police londonienne, précisant que les hommes seraient relâchés lundi. "Ils restent pleinement visés par l'enquête tandis que nous explorons plusieurs pistes", a-t-il également indiqué, ajoutant que les cinq individus, suspectés d'infractions à la législation relative aux explosifs et de projet d'acte terroriste, seraient soumis à un strict contrôle judiciaire. Les autorités avaient auparavant fait savoir que les suspects étaient tous des ressortissants britanniques originaires de Londres et âgés d'une vingtaine d'années. Avant l'annonce de leur libération sous caution, une source proche de l'enquête a déclaré à Reuters qu'un mobile lié à l'Iran était considéré comme le plus probable, même si la piste d'une opération de sabotage russe ou d'un complot islamiste est également examinée. DES HOMMES "CAGOULÉS ET MASQUÉS" COURANT À TRAVERS CHAMPS L'ambassade d'Iran, dans un communiqué publié sur le réseau X, a évoqué des "spéculations infondées et malveillantes", ajoutant qu'elle "rejetait catégoriquement et condamnait fermement" toute tentative de relier Téhéran aux arrestations et que de telles spéculations ne feraient qu'"alimenter la propagande iranophobe" au Royaume-Uni. Laurence Tayor, sans explicitement mentionner l'Iran, a dit avoir conscience du vif intérêt que suscite un éventuel lien entre le contexte géopolitique actuel et cet incident. "Soyez assurés que nous examinons cette affaire sous tous les angles possibles, y compris l'hypothèse qu'elle ait été activement menée par des intermédiaires ou par des individus travaillant, sciemment ou non, pour le compte d'un État étranger." Le président américain Donald Trump a déclaré dimanche que les suspects avaient tenté de causer "d'importants dégâts" et qu'ils avaient fait l'objet d'une surveillance de la part des autorités britanniques et américaines, affirmation qui a questionné certains médias britanniques compte tenu de la proximité des hommes avec la base au moment de leur arrestation. La source proche de l'enquête a précisé que celle-ci n'était pas le résultat d'un renseignement préalable, bien que les mesures de sécurité aient été renforcées autour de la base. L'agricultrice ayant alerté la police, dont l'identité n'a pas été révélée, a indiqué à la BBC avoir vu un groupe d'"hommes cagoulés et masqués" courir à travers champs, estimant que son appel au numéro d'urgence 999 avait à lui seul "fait échouer leurs plans". RÉUNION DU COMITÉ DE CRISE GOUVERNEMENTAL Le ministre de la Défense, Wes Streeting, a déclaré à la BBC que l'agricultrice n'avait qu'une "vision partielle" de la situation, ajoutant qu'il ne spéculerait pas sur les motifs d'une enquête en cours. Evoquant la menace iranienne qui pèse globalement sur le pays, il a toutefois déclaré : "Nous savons que l'Iran et ses relais veulent nous nuire. Nous savons qu'ils haïssent notre démocratie, et nous savons que nous devons régulièrement déjouer les tentatives iraniennes visant à menacer soit nos intérêts, soit nos alliés." Le Premier ministre Andy Burnham a annoncé qu'il présiderait plus tard lundi une réunion du comité gouvernemental chargé de la gestion des situations d'urgence (Cobra). Le gouvernement britannique a autorisé les États-Unis à utiliser des bombardiers basés à Fairford pour frapper des sites de missiles iraniens qui attaquaient des navires dans le détroit d'Ormuz. Les Gardiens de la révolution iraniens avaient averti Londres en juillet de ne pas le faire, ajoutant que toute base utilisée pour lancer des attaques deviendrait une cible légitime. L'AMBASSADE US ÉMET UNE ALERTE DE SÉCURITÉ La Grande-Bretagne a relevé en avril son niveau national de menace terroriste de "substantiel" à "grave", après une série d'incidents antisémites dans le nord de Londres, indiquant qu'une attaque terroriste dans les six prochains mois était considérée comme hautement probable. La police a dit enquêter sur des connexions avec l'Iran dans de nombreux incidents au cours desquels des biens liés à la communauté juive ou à des dissidents iraniens ont été pris pour cible. En réaction aux arrestations de Fairford, l'ambassade des États-Unis a publié une alerte de sécurité recommandant aux citoyens américains de "faire preuve de prudence" et d'être "attentifs à leur sécurité personnelle". "Les installations, rassemblements et organisations liés aux États-Unis pourraient être exposés à un risque accru", selon cette alerte. À Fairford, la police a établi un périmètre de sécurité de 400 mètres autour de la base et évacué les habitants de 85 logements du village voisin de Whelford, dont les autorités ont indiqué lundi qu'ils allaient bientôt pouvoir regagner leur domicile.

item.title: BCE-Une réponse mesurée reste appropriée pour juguler l'inflation, dit Lagarde
item.description: Une réponse mesurée reste appropriée pour contenir la hausse des prix, a déclaré lundi la présidente de la Banque centrale européenne, Christine Lagarde, l'inflation enregistrée cette année n'ayant pas encore entraîné d'effets de second tour dans la zone euro.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Une réponse mesurée reste appropriée pour contenir la hausse des prix, a déclaré lundi la présidente de la Banque centrale européenne, Christine Lagarde, l'inflation enregistrée cette année n'ayant pas encore entraîné d'effets de second tour dans la zone euro. L'inflation en zone euro a déjà dépassé les 3% et pourrait avoisiner les 4% d’ici la fin de l’année, soit le double de l’objectif fixé par Francfort, ce qui alimente les paris des marchés selon lesquels jusqu’à quatre hausses de taux supplémentaires seront nécessaires l’année prochaine, en plus des deux déjà décidées en juin et début septembre. Christine Lagarde a fait valoir que la flambée des prix du pétrole et du gaz, liée au conflit entre les États-Unis et l’Iran, était le principal facteur à l’origine de la hausse des prix. "Nous anticipons une hausse de l’inflation, mais ne voyons pour l’instant aucun signe indiquant qu’elle s’installe durablement", a-t-elle déclaré lors d'une audition devant une commission du Parlement européen à Bruxelles. "À ce stade, nous ne disposons d’aucun élément indiquant que les prix de l’énergie se répercutent sur les salaires." "Cela signifie que, même si le choc est trop important pour être ignoré, nous estimons qu’une réponse mesurée est appropriée pour contenir l’inflation", a-t-elle ajouté. Christine Lagarde a toutefois reconnu que les risques penchaient en faveur d’une inflation plus élevée et que les perspectives étaient entachées d’une forte incertitude. Bien que la notion de "réponse mesurée" reste floue, les économistes estiment que les deux premières hausses de taux, espacées de trois mois, constituent un bon indicateur. Par conséquent, de nombreux économistes s’attendent à ce que la BCE s’abstienne d’agir lors de sa réunion du 29 octobre et ne procède à une hausse qu’en décembre, lors de la publication des nouvelles projections. Selon les données LSEG, les marchés anticipent à 57% la probabilité d'un maintien des taux par la BCE fin octobre. Christine Lagarde a souligné avec optimisme que le secteur manufacturier affichait de solides performances, que le marché du travail restait robuste et que l’investissement devrait également soutenir la croissance.

item.title: Jensen Huang's invisible hand is tied on AI safety
item.description: As a regulation debate rages, Nvidia's boss unveiled tools to monitor and shut down rogue agents. They should help rebuild some trust, but an accompanying $150 bln stock-buyback hike lays bare the financial incentives. A quest for rapid progress means self-policing isn't enough.
item.dc:creator: Robert Cyran
item.content:encoded: As a regulation debate rages, Nvidia's boss unveiled tools to monitor and shut down rogue agents. They should help rebuild some trust, but an accompanying $150 bln stock-buyback hike lays bare the financial incentives. A quest for rapid progress means self-policing isn't enough. Full view will be published shortly. Follow Robert Cyran on Bluesky . Nvidia on September 28 unveiled tools it says will prevent AI agents from acting in an unauthorized manner and could have prevented the Hugging Face attack by OpenAI agents. One product is OpenShell, which limits actions AI agents can take and what they can access. It is open source and runs on hardware from both Nvidia and other manufacturers. The other is Sentry, which Nvidia says monitors what happens in OpenShell and shuts down an agent quickly if it is drifting from its intended task or operating constraints. Sentry runs on Nvidia Bluefield processing units. Nvidia also said on September 28 that its board authorized a $150 billion increase to its existing share repurchase program, bringing it to $235 billion. The company plans to complete the buybacks by the end of its 2028 fiscal year on January 31, 2028. CONTEXT-NEWS

Con 384 sezioni scrutinate su 487, Fabio Roscioli è avanti con il 52,47% dei voti, davanti a Frank Benedetto del centrosinistra al 36,11%, mentre Domenico Giannetta, candidato di Futuro Nazionale sostenuto da Vannacci, è al 10,04%. item.title: Italy's Meloni passes by-election test against new far-right rival
item.description: Italy's ruling coalition won a closely watched by-election in the southern region of Calabria on Monday, the first major test for Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni against a new far-right foe ahead of a general election due next year.
item.dc:creator: Angelo Amante
item.content:encoded: Italy's ruling coalition won a closely watched by-election in the southern region of Calabria on Monday, the first major test for Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni against a new far-right foe ahead of a general election due next year. [USN:L1N44T0CD TEXT:"National Future"], led by former army general Roberto Vannacci, has surged to around 9% in opinion polls since its launch in February, overtaking Meloni's junior coalition partners and challenging the right in the conservative constituency of Reggio Calabria. However, the party's bid fell short, with the government candidate taking about 53% of the vote, while Vannacci's nominee secured roughly 10%, according to a partial count. Analysts had predicted a stronger showing for Vannacci in a traditionally rightist stronghold, saying he might have split the right-wing vote and handed victory to the centre-left. "We won by a landslide," Roberto Occhiuto, governor of Calabria and deputy leader of the coalition party Forza Italia, said in a video posted on X. AI-MANIPULATED IMAGE Support for Vannacci has grown nationwide on the back of his [USN:L8N44V0OK TEXT:"anti-migrant rhetoric"] and calls for what he describes as traditional Italian values. His rise has unsettled Meloni and could complicate her re-election prospects, drawing away voters who backed her coalition at the last national ballot in 2022. Pollsters have said she could keep hold of power if she forged an alliance with Vannacci. But any such tie-up would cause tension within government ranks. Parliament undersecretary Matilde Siracusano, a Forza Italia lawmaker and Occhiuto's partner, warned that any electoral pact with National Future would pose "a serious problem". She has said she will sue Vannacci after he posted an AI-generated image on social media showing her wearing a revealing, low-cut top. The centre-left candidate in the by-election won about 35% of the vote, improving on the bloc's performance in 2022, although turnout was just 22% against 49.4% four years ago. "With turnout extremely low, strong media attention and a candidate with significant personal backing, I believe Vannacci expected a far better showing," said Lorenzo Pregliasco, the head of polling firm YouTrend. Vannacci himself did not immediately comment on the result.

item.title: Nvidia settles trademark lawsuit over 'Modulus' AI software
item.description: Nvidia has settled a trademark lawsuit brought by financial technology company Modulus Financial Engineering over Nvidia's "Modulus" AI software, according to a filing in Austin, Texas federal court.
item.dc:creator: Blake Brittain
item.content:encoded: Nvidia (NVDA.O) has settled a trademark lawsuit brought by financial technology company Modulus Financial Engineering over Nvidia's "Modulus" AI software, according to a filing in Austin, Texas federal court. The companies told the court on Friday that they have resolved their dispute and asked to pause the case while they finalize their agreement Spokespeople for the companies did not immediately respond to requests for comment and more details on the settlement on Monday Modulus Financial [USN:L2N3GH16E TEXT:"filed the lawsuit"] in 2024, alleging that Nvidia's Modulus open-source software for developing AI machine-learning models would confuse consumers Scottsdale, Arizona-based Modulus Financial has provided financial software to companies including JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, and Goldman Sachs since 1997, according to its website, and its lawsuit said it has "become widely recognized for its leadership and innovation — including within the field of A.I." Nvidia denied the allegations and said in a court filing earlier this year that it changed its software's name to "Nvidia PhysicsNeMo" in 2025 The case had been scheduled to go to trial next month The case is Modulus Financial Engineering Inc v. Nvidia Corp, US District Court for the Western District of Texas, No. 1:24-cv-00362. item.title: Legrand raises mid-term targets on data centre growth
item.description: French electrical and digital building infrastructure group Legrand raised its medium-term targets on Monday, driven by a stronger-than-expected growth in its data centre business.
item.dc:creator: Mathias Rozario, Rihab Latrache
item.content:encoded: French electrical and digital building infrastructure group Legrand (LEGD.PA) raised its medium-term targets on Monday, driven by a stronger-than-expected growth in its data centre business. Legrand, which operates across the commercial, industrial and residential sectors, has been outpacing the 2030 goals since it announced them in 2024, thanks to soaring demand for data centres, which account for a growing share of its revenue, CEO Benoit Coquart told Reuters. It now expects average organic revenue growth of 6% to 8% per year between 2027 and 2030, up from the 3% to 5% range it had forecast for 2025-2030. It also sees an adjusted operating margin averaging between 21% and 22% of total sales, versus around 20% in the previous guidance. Coquart expects the sector's boom to continue in the coming years, saying Legrand's clients are bolstering their AI investment plans even as some AI leaders [USN:L1N45403R TEXT:"urge developers"] to slow the development of advanced models. "We currently have 80 gigawatts of installed capacity in data centres for IT, and we believe that by 2030, this will rise to 180," Coquart said in an interview ahead of Tuesday's Capital Markets Day. The group expects the share of turnover generated by its historical building business to shrink, while the energy and digital transition business, which includes data centre infrastructure and energy management solutions, is set to grow from 53% of its total revenue in 2025 to around 70% by 2030. "There are three factors: acquisitions, which will mainly be in the energy and digital transition sectors; the divestment, which will take place in the core business; and, quite simply, the different rates of organic growth," Coquart said. Legrand expects its construction business to return to moderate growth of between 1% and 3% in Europe. The situation is slightly less positive in the US for both residential and commercial business areas, he added.

item.title: Energy Watch: Big Oil's big rethink
item.description: After a whirlwind of speeches, threats, peace overtures and a summit between the US and Chinese leaders in Washington last week, the US-Iran standoff remains pretty stagnant. But not entirely.
item.dc:creator: Ron Bousso
item.content:encoded: After a whirlwind of speeches, threats, peace overtures and a summit between the US and Chinese leaders in Washington last week, the US-Iran standoff remains pretty stagnant. But not entirely. Oil prices [USN:L4N45J03L TEXT:"rebounded"] by around 3% to above $107 a barrel on Monday morning after President Donald Trump [USN:L6N45I080 TEXT:"rejected a peace deal"] from Iran that would have reopened the Strait of Hormuz. While this has again dashed hopes of a breakthrough, oil flows through the critical waterway [USN:L1N45J07E TEXT:"have grown steadily"] in recent weeks, suggesting that both sides are for now comfortable with the status quo. Elevated oil prices are stoking concerns of persistently higher global inflation, increasing expectations that central banks will push up interest rates. Government [USN:L6N45F0LQ TEXT:"bond yields"] last week soared to new multi-decade highs, aggravated by hot US business activity data and rising government debt concerns. The energy and financial markets also continue to question whether the Trump administration will impose a ban on diesel exports in the coming weeks in an attempt to lower soaring diesel prices, which rose above $6.50 a gallon ahead of the November midterm elections. After holding talks with American refiners last week, the administration seems to be searching for [USN:L1N45G0Q3 TEXT:"an alternative to a short-term ban"]. The possibility of a ban is already having an impact on the market, as the [USN:L6N45G0YB TEXT:"gap between US crude oil futures"] and the global Brent benchmark has widened, a signal that markets expect US refiners to process less crude oil if their diesel output gets stuck at home. Exactly seven months since the start of the Mideast conflict, the energy markets are slowly acknowledging that many of the war’s consequences could linger for far longer than initially anticipated. This is fundamentally changing the strategic calculus for the world’s oil and gas majors. [USN:L6N45H0N6 TEXT:"More on this in my latest column"]. In other news: Lower standards: The US Transportation Department on Monday will finalize [USN:FWN45I08D TEXT:"sharply lower vehicle fuel economy standards"] through 2031, reversing a push by the Biden administration to force automakers to build more electric vehicles. Energy shock: The European Union is [USN:S8N42Q0E1 TEXT:"facing an energy price crisis"] as fallout from the Iran war roils oil and gas markets, EU Energy Commissioner Dan Jorgensen said in a letter seen by Reuters that urged countries to consider measures to curb natural gas demand. Gas shock: At the same time, the CEO of German gas importer VNG, Ulf Heitmueller, said that even though Europe’s biggest economy is heading into winter with unusually low natural gas stocks, it faces [USN:L8N45G0QN TEXT:"no immediate supply risk"] thanks to a broader and more resilient import portfolio than during the 2022 energy crisis. AI trading boom: The Iran conflict has put a spotlight on the murky world of refined fuel trading as the world battles constrained supply and record-high prices. But AI may bring the trading of diesel, gasoline and other products out of the shadows for good, [USN:L1N45G07L TEXT:"explains ROI Asia Commodities Columnist Clyde Russell"]. item.title: French far-right leader Bardella denies media claim he made antisemitic remarks
item.description: French far-right leader Jordan Bardella on Monday denied a report by investigative website Mediapart alleging he made antisemitic remarks in private messages over a decade ago, calling the allegations "crude fabrications".
item.dc:creator: Michel Rose
item.content:encoded: French far-right leader Jordan Bardella on Monday denied a report by investigative website Mediapart alleging he made antisemitic remarks in private messages over a decade ago, calling the allegations "crude fabrications". The report comes as Bardella's far-right National Rally (RN) party, whose presidential candidate Marine Le Pen is leading polls ahead of next year's election, seeks to clear its racist image and build close ties with Israel. "I formally dispute the accusations against me by Mediapart, which attributes to me deranged and antisemitic remarks that I supposedly made when I was a minor. These are obviously crude forgeries," Bardella wrote on X. He said he had instructed his lawyer to pursue "all necessary proceedings" against Mediapart. Mediapart, in a report published on Monday, said it had reviewed dozens of private messages from 2013-2015 - the early years of Bardella's career in the National Front, the forerunner of the RN - that it said showed a pattern of antisemitic and conspiratorial rhetoric. Mediapart cited one message in which it said Bardella claimed "all the banks are owned by Jews". The left-leaning outlet, which has a long history of unearthing political scandals in France, said it had independently authenticated the private messages, and had also drawn on testimony from former party colleagues, which it named with first names and the initial of their last names. Bardella, 31, has become the face of the RN's decade-long effort to "de-demonise", or normalise, its image. He was the party's de facto presidential candidate until July, when an appeals court cleared Le Pen to run for the presidency, and will be France's prime minister if she wins next year's vote. Le Pen, speaking with reporters on Monday, said she believed the report could "only be a fake, a manipulation, a dirty trick". She said she expected Bardella to file an imminent defamation lawsuit, adding she had nothing to discuss with her young protege. A Monday poll showed her coming first in next April's first round vote and beating both leftist and centrist candidates in a May runoff. A slew of antisemitic, Islamophobic and racist comments by some RN candidates derailed the party's hopes of winning a parliamentary majority in France's legislative vote in 2024. Bardella at the time pledged to avoid such "casting errors" in the future by systematically kicking out any candidates with a history of toxic statements.
